questions.stem: Which of the following drugs crosses the blood-brain barrier?
questions.solutionHtml:
Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier.

It is a naturally occurring aromatic amino acid and an immediate precursor of dopamine that can cross the blood-brain barrier. Dopamine does not cross the blood-brain barrier because of the polar nature of the molecule. Levodopa is also a polar compound but it can cross the blood-brain barrier through an aromatic amino acid transporter.

Therefore, levodopa is used therapeutically when dopamine is required for central action. Levodopa is converted to dopamine by the decarboxylase enzyme.

Carbidopa is a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor and does not penetrate the blood-brain barrier.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 330

questions.stem: A 55-year-old is diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and is started on levodopa therapy. Which of the following statements is incorrect about the drug?

options.label: A
options.text: In parkinsonism, phenothiazines reduce its efficacy

options.label: C
options.text: Pyridoxine reduces effect of levodopa in parkinsonism

options.label: D
options.text: Domperidone reduces levodopa induced emesis and its therapeutic potential

questions.answerText: Domperidone reduces levodopa induced emesis and its therapeutic potential
questions.solutionHtml:
Domperidone is an antidopaminergic antiemetic that can reverse levodopa-induced emesis without affecting the therapeutic potential as it cannot cross the blood-brain barrier.

The antiemetic effect is through its action on CTZ which is outside the blood-brain barrier.

Option A: Typical antipsychotics like phenothiazines can reduce the efficacy of levodopa because of its central D2 blocking property.

Option B: Levodopa is a prodrug. It is converted into dopamine by the decarboxylase enzyme in CNS.

Option C: Pyridoxine can reduce the effect of levodopa by increasing its peripheral conversion to dopamine by potentiating peripheral dopa decarboxylase enzyme.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 495

questions.stem: After initiation of levodopa therapy, a 55-year-old patient starts experiencing adverse effects. Which of these side effects is not decreased by the addition of carbidopa?
questions.solutionHtml:
Behavioral adverse effects like confusion, hallucinations, nightmares, delusions, postural hypotension are not reduced after the addition of carbidopa.

In fact, they are increased in patients who are taking levodopa with peripheral decarboxylase inhibitors. This is because higher levels of dopamine are formed in CNS.

The combination of levodopa with peripheral decarboxylase inhibitors like carbidopa inhibits peripheral adverse effects of dopamine. This decreases the adverse effects like:

  • Anorexia, nausea, and vomiting 
  • Cardiac arrhythmias
  • On and off effect of motor performance




Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no 487
Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, Page no 496
K.D Tripathi - Essentials of medical pharmacology 8th Edition, Page no :455, 457

questions.stem: A 60-year-old male is brought to the casualty in a confused state. On examination, he has severe muscle rigidity. His son says that the patient is on treatment for Parkinson's disease but has forgotten to take his medication as they went on a holiday trip. What is the likely diagnosis in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Abrupt withdrawal of levodopa or dopaminergic agonists can precipitate neuroleptic malignant syndrome. It is characterized by extreme rigidity, confusion, and hyperthermia. 

It is an emergency condition that can turn fatal if immediate intervention is not done. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is commonly associated with the use of typical antipsychotics.

Option A: Wearing off phenomenon - Each dose of levodopa improves mobility for a period of 1-2 hours. After that, the effect of the drug wears off, and rigidity and akinesia return. This can be surpassed by increasing the dosing and frequency.

Option B: On/off phenomenon - Rapid fluctuation between on and off periods.

  • On period: When the patient has a beneficial effect of the medications but with disabling dyskinesias
  • Off period: No beneficial effects from anti-Parkinsonism medications.

'Wearing off' and 'On / Off' phenomenon occur with long-term treatment of levodopa.

Option D: Serotonin syndrome occurs with co-prescription of MAO-inhibitors and SSRIs. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 331

questions.stem: A patient on long-term treatment with levodopa and carbidopa for Parkinson's disease is diagnosed with on/off phenomenon. Which of the following drugs is used to treat this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Safinamide is used for the treatment of the on/off phenomenon.

Management of On/Off phenomenon:

  • To prolong the 'On' phase:
    • COMT inhibitor - entacapone, tolcapone
    • Irreversible MAO-B inhibitor - selegiline, rasagiline
    • Reversible MAO-B inhibitor - safinamide.
  • Rescue from 'Off' phase: injection apomorphine

Dopaminergic agonists like pramipexole, ropinirole, and rotigotine are also effective in the treatment of the on/off phenomenon.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 337

questions.stem: A patient who is on levodopa therapy presents with confusion, delusions of grandeur, and hallucinations. What is the most appropriate treatment for his condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of levodopa-induced psychosis for which quetiapine is the most appropriate treatment.

Quetiapine and clozapine are the two atypical antipsychotics that are most effective and best tolerated in levodopa-induced psychosis. 

Typical antipsychotics are effective against levodopa-induced psychosis but may cause marked worsening of parkinsonism. Hence, atypical antipsychotics are deemed safer. 





Journal, Pharmacy and therapeutics; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5440097/
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 418

questions.stem: While discharging a patient with Parkinson's disease, the treating physician writes a prescription of levodopa along with another drug that can increase the bioavailability of the former. Identify the drug.
questions.solutionHtml:
Entacapone is a peripheral COMT inhibitor that increases the bioavailability of levodopa.

It inhibits the peripheral metabolism of levodopa thereby increasing the bioavailability of levodopa.  

Options B and D: Ropinirole and apomorphine are dopamine receptor agonists and do not have any significant effect on levodopa bioavailability.

Option C: Amantadine which is an antiviral drug is also anti-Parkinsonian due to its varied actions including increased release and decreased uptake of dopamine. It has no significant effect on the bioavailability of levodopa.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 332

questions.stem: Which of the following anti-Parkinsonism drugs is correctly matched with its mechanism of action?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tolcapone and entacapone are selective, potent, and reversible COMT (catechol-O-methyl transferase) inhibitors.

COMT metabolizes levodopa and blockade of this pathway prolongs the half-life of levodopa and allows a larger fraction of the administered dose to reach the brain.

Option B: Rasagiline is a selective MAO-B inhibitor.

Option C: Amantadine acts by antagonism of the NMDA type of glutamate receptors.

Option D: Apomorphine is a dopaminergic agonist that is FDA-approved as a 'rescue therapy' for the acute intermittent treatment of 'off' episodes.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 332

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false regarding the use of selegiline in Parkinsonism?

options.label: A
options.text: It acts as a selective MAO A inhibitor

options.label: B
options.text: Incidence of cheese reaction is minimal

options.label: C
options.text: May be used for on / off phenomenon

questions.answerText: It acts as a selective MAO A inhibitor
questions.solutionHtml:
Selegiline acts as a selective MAO-B inhibitor.

At higher doses, MAO-A can also be inhibited. Higher doses are used for depression and administered in the form of the transdermal patch. 

Option B: Selective MAO-B inhibitors do not interfere significantly with the peripheral metabolism of dietary amines and do not cause cheese reaction.

Option C:  It has lower efficacy than levodopa but when added with levodopa it prolongs its action and also decreases the wearing-off effect of levodopa.

Option D: Selegiline forms metabolites like amphetamine and methamphetamine that can result in anxiety, insomnia, and other undesirable effects. Rasagiline, unlike selegiline, does not form amphetamines as metabolites.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 332

questions.stem: Which of the following dopamine agonists is an ergot derivative?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bromocriptine and pergolide are ergot derivatives that act as potent agonists at the D2 receptor.

Pramipexole and ropinirole are non-ergot derivatives having D2/D3 receptor agonistic action. They are better tolerated and have fewer GI symptoms than bromocriptine.

Dopamine agonists can be classified as follows:

  • Ergot derivatives - Bromocriptine, pergolide, cabergoline
  • Non-ergot derivatives - Pramipexole, ropinirole, apomorphine, rotigotine

Dopaminergic agonists exert subtype-selective activation of dopaminergic receptors involved in the Parkinsonism circuit of the striatum.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 498

questions.stem: A 50-year-old female patient visits the OPD with complaints of burning sensation associated with an irresistible urge to move her legs since 2 weeks. It occurs especially at night and the discomfort gets relieved on moving her legs. Which is the first-line drug that can be prescribed for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
The symptoms in this patient are suggestive of restless leg syndrome and gabapentin is the first-line choice of treatment for this condition.    

Restless leg syndrome is a typical sensory-motor disorder that generally affects the legs during rest periods, especially sleep. There is an irresistible urge to shake the legs associated with burning sensation, itching, and cramps of the legs. In idiopathic cases, dopaminergic hypofunction is postulated.

In patients with restless legs syndrome, iron stores are initially repleted, and the aggravating factors are eliminated. If RLS still persists, initial therapy with a gabapentinoid (pregabalin, gabapentin, gabapentin enacarbil) are preferred, rather than a dopamine agonist (pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine). This is due to the high frequency of intermediate and long-term augmentation with dopamine agonists, as well as their risk of impulse control disorders.

FDA-approved drugs for the treatment of restless leg syndrome: 

  • Gabapentin
  • Ropinirole
  • Pramipexole
  • Rotigotine 

A dopamine agonist is used as an alternative in patients with increased risk for side effects from gabapentinoids, such as those with obesity and its complications, a past or present history of moderate to severe depression, a disorder causing gait instability or respiratory failure, and a history of substance use disorder.

Option A: Benztropine is an anticholinergic that can be used for drug-induced parkinsonism. 

Option C: Riluzole is a benzothiazole derivative that is used in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

Option D: Benzodiazepines like clonazepam can be used as co-adjuvant drugs in the treatment of restless leg syndrome but should not be used as first-line therapy.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 507
Online Resource, https://www.uptodate.com/contents/management-of-restless-legs-syndrome-and-periodic-limb-movement-disorder-in-adults#H1935612

questions.stem: Which of the following dopamine receptor agonists has antioxidant properties?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pramipexole is a dopamine receptor agonist that has an additional antioxidant effect. 

Pramipexole has a possible neuroprotective effect by its ability to scavenge hydrogen peroxide and enhance neurotrophic activity. 





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 498

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs would you prescribe as a transdermal patch to patients with Parkinson’s disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rotigotine is a dopamine agonist used in Parkinson’s disease as a transdermal patch.

A transdermal patch can lead to various local reactions at the application site. Rotigotine was withdrawn from some markets due to crystal formation on the patch but later reintroduced with a newer formulation.

Selegiline transdermal patch is approved for depression and not for Parkinson’s disease.





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Pag no 489
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, page no 331

questions.stem: A 30-year-old female is on treatment with ropinirole for restless leg syndrome. Which of the following adverse effects are not expected to be seen in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cardiac fibrosis is a side effect of pergolide, not ropinirole. 

The adverse effects of ropinirole include: 

  • Nausea
  • Drowsiness
  • Postural hypotension
  • Hallucinations

Cardiac and pleural fibrosis are seen with pergolide which is also a dopamine agonist. Pergolide was withdrawn from the market due to reports of serious valve damage.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 498
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 332

questions.stem: Which anti-Parkinsonism drug is an NMDA-glutamate receptor antagonist?
questions.solutionHtml:
Amantadine which is an antiviral agent, also used in parkinsonism has NMDA glutamate receptor antagonist action. 

This action is responsible for its antidyskinetic properties. It also promotes presynaptic synthesis and release of dopamine. 

Option B: Rotigotine is a dopamine agonist available as a transdermal patch.

Options C and D: Benzhexol and trihexyphenidyl are central anticholinergics.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 332

questions.stemHtml: A 55-year-old patient presents to the dermatology OPD with findings as shown in the image below. Which of the following drugs can result in this adverse effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
The above presentation is of livedo reticularis, which is an adverse effect of amantadine.

The patient presents with a common skin finding consisting of a mottled vesicular pattern that appears as a lace-like purplish discoloration of the skin which is due to the local release of catecholamines resulting in post-capillary vasoconstriction.

Adverse effects of amantadine are:

  • Insomnia, restlessness, confusion
  • Nightmares
  • Anticholinergic effects
  • Hallucinations 
  • Livedo reticularis
  • Edema of ankles




Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 501

questions.stem: Which is the 5HT2A inverse agonist approved for use in psychosis associated with Parkinsonism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pimavanserin is a selective 5-HT2A receptor inverse agonist that is approved for the management of delirium and hallucinations associated with Parkinson's disease.

Option A: Lorcaserin is a 5-HT2C agonist indicated as an anti-obesity agent. 

Option C: Pitolisant is an H3 receptor inverse agonist approved for the treatment of narcolepsy.

Option D: Mianserin is an anti-depressant.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 497
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 300

questions.stem: A 30-year-old male patient presented to the casualty department with bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremors. His attender reported that he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and had recently started treatment. What is the drug of choice to treat the patient's presenting symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of drug-induced parkinsonism, for which the drug of choice is benzhexol, also known as trihexiphenidyl. 

Drug-induced parkinsonism is caused by certain drugs that have D2 antagonistic action, such as typical antipsychotics. Due to the decrease in dopaminergic activity, they result in an unbalanced cholinergic activity. Benzhexol is a centrally acting antimuscarinic agent. It acts by restoring the cholinergic balance in the striatal interneurons.



The following drugs are implicated in drug-induced parkinsonism:

Drug class

Examples 
Typical antipsychotics

Phenothiazines, haloperidol
Atypical antipsychotics Risperidone, olanzapine
Dopamine depleters Reserpine, tetrabenazine
Antiemetics Metoclopramide, levosulpiride
Calcium channel blockers Flunarizine, cinnarizine




Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page No. 503
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page No. 332
